subject: Throughput sizing follow-up: latency targets, tokens/sec, peak vs steady
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@finex.com>, Nina Patel <nina.patel@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps - throughput / latency qualification

Thanks again for the call earlier today — appreciate the walkthrough of the Finex streaming assistant workload. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can size Dedicated capacity and confirm SLOs:

Summary of requirements from call:
- Latency target: p95 <= 150ms for interactive streaming responses (client streaming enabled).
- Steady-state: ~40 QPS (concurrent sessions ~80 with client-side multiplexing).
- Peak: short spikes up to 220 concurrent sessions (~150 QPS) during market open (approx 08:00-09:00 ET) lasting ~10-20 minutes.
- Typical response lengths: 600-1200 tokens; some long reports up to 6k tokens (batch offline).
- Model: open-roberta-stream-v2 (we discussed possible switch to a smaller ref model for low-latency paths).

Requests / next steps:
1) Can you send an anonymized workload snapshot (example logs with request sizes, tokens per request, timestamps) for 24-48 hours so we can compute tokens/sec and peak concurrency? CSV is fine.
2) Confirm whether streaming is required end-to-end (we'll assume yes unless you specify otherwise).
3) Any hard SLA constraints around p99 or only p95?

I can turn around an initial sizing doc (GPU counts, expected tokens/sec, recommended quantization + batching settings) once we have the workload snapshot. We’ll attach a concise recommendation PDF with a couple of config options (latency-first, cost-optimized).

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick follow-up if useful.

--
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps - throughput / latency qualification

Rafael — thanks for the summary. Attaching a 48h sample (anonymized) of request traces: finex-workload-snapshot.csv. Quick answers inline:

- Streaming: yes, streaming is required for the interactive assistant. We stream partial tokens as they are generated.
- p99: not a hard SLA today; p95 is most important.
- Model: currently running a tuned open-roberta-stream-v2; we're open to exploring lighter variants for the streaming path if it helps latency.

Snapshot highlights (from our side):
- Avg QPS (steady): 38-45 across trading hours.
- Peak QPS: 148 (observed spike on 2026-03-03 08:12:00 ET) with ~210 concurrent sessions reported in our frontend telemetry (short ~12m duration).
- Median tokens per response: 720; 95th percentile ~ 2100 tokens.

Let us know your sizing assumptions and if you need additional telemetry (e.g., KB of request+response payloads, network RTT).

Samir
Lead Platform Eng, Finex Corp
samir@finex.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps - throughput / latency qualification

Samir — got the CSV, thanks. I ran a quick pass and attached a short sizing recommendation (redwood-sizing-recommendation.pdf) with two options:

Option A — Latency-first (recommended if p95 <= 150ms is strict):
- Runtime: 4x A100-equivalent GPU nodes (dedicated pool) with per-node concurrency cap ~48 streaming sessions.
- Expected sustained throughput: ~220k tokens/sec aggregate across pool (~55k tokens/sec per GPU) depending on quantization.
- Expected p95: ~120-150ms for 700-token responses with streaming enabled and prefix caching for repeated prompts.
- Notes: Use int8 quantization + kernel selection for attention optimizations; keep batching small to preserve tail latency.

Option B — Cost-optimized:
- Runtime: 2x A100-equivalent GPU nodes with burst autoscaling to 4 during peak windows.
- Expected sustained throughput: ~110k tokens/sec aggregate; p95 ~180-220ms on heavier responses.
- Notes: More aggressive batching and larger batch windows; recommend moving long-form report generation to a separate offline job.

Assumptions I used (from your CSV): avg response 720 tokens, steady QPS 40, peak 150 QPS over short windows. If you want to target p99 we'll need a wider headroom (add ~30-50% capacity).

Next steps from Redwood side:
- Rafael + Marissa to run a targeted microbenchmark against your anonymized traces in our staging to validate p95 numbers (need a short replay harness).
- If you're comfortable, provide a sanitized set of 1,000 full traces (include tokenization) and we’ll run the replay.
- Schedule a sizing validation call next week — propose Tue 2026-03-16 10:00 PT.

Attached: redwood-sizing-recommendation.pdf (2 pages)

--
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

- We've shared the 1,000 sanitized traces (SFTP link in separate email) — you should have access.
- We confirm streaming is required for the main assistant path; background batch jobs can be moved offline.
- p95 <= 150ms is a firm target for the interactive path; p99 is nice-to-have but not mandatory today.

Proposed actions:
1) Redwood to run microbenchmark against the sanitized traces and share results by EOD Fri (2026-03-20).
2) Joint call to review sizing and trade-offs on Tue 2026-03-23 10:00 PT.
3) If numbers look good, we'll start drafting a Dedicated capacity PO for the latency-first option.
